nodes.label: Falsification program (37 pre-registered attempts, 0 passes of the high-return bar)
nodes.rationale: Thirty-seven pre-registered attempts across nine equity families plus credit, non-equity trend and market-neutral relative value; search phase closed 2026-08-03 at 37 attempts, with a 38th pre-registered run (M12, a diagnostic) after the close - the two numbers are reconciled in HANDOFF and docs/trial_log.json. The discipline of how it failed is the deliverable, not an equity curve.

nodes.label: Pre-registration (rules committed to git before the code that produces results)
nodes.rationale: Paired with honest kill-criteria (no re-tuning a failed run) and out-of-sample / out-of-regime tests, culminating in an international test on five independent markets and a survivorship-aware stock test, neither used to design anything.
nodes.norm_label: pre-registration (rules committed to git before the code that produces results)

nodes.label: Honest conclusion (no robust, regime-independent, cost-surviving high-return EOD strategy)
nodes.rationale: Across seven plausible families: 0 passes of the high-return bar; one weak risk-adjusted pass (VIX term structure, forward-paper only), one blocked on data, one deferred. The only run that ever cleared 15%/yr (E16, 16.8%) did so on a survivorship-flattered universe with a 66% drawdown - a textbook artifact. The one partly-deployable result, a 1x 200-day-MA rotation, is a market-dependent risk-management overlay, not a return engine.
nodes.norm_label: honest conclusion (no robust, regime-independent, cost-surviving high-return eod strategy)

No code path in this repo can reach a funded account; no real money, no dashboard. The series exists to accumulate out-of-sample evidence the backtests cannot provide.

nodes.label: Capstone Synthesis — Swing-Trading Falsification Program
nodes.author: Evan Daruwalla
nodes.rationale: Single standing document accounting for what the program set out to do, how it was run, and what it found; synthesizes the append-only record, which remains ground truth for dated detail.

nodes.label: Pre-registration Before Code
nodes.rationale: Rules, windows and full PASS/FAIL criteria are git-committed doc-only before the runner exists, so the commit hash provably predates the analysis. No criterion is ever relaxed after seeing results; a FAIL is never re-tuned into a pass.

nodes.label: Asymmetric Falsification on a Survivor Universe
nodes.rationale: The universe is biased in the strategy's favor, so survivorship and any lookahead can only help. Therefore only a FAIL is clean; a PASS is UNINTERPRETABLE and routes to forward paper, never a live claim.
nodes.norm_label: asymmetric falsification on a survivor universe

nodes.label: D1 Dual-Bar Verdict
nodes.rationale: Two pre-registered pass tiers plus FAIL, all three outcomes fixed before each run so no verdict can be invented after the numbers land.

nodes.label: PASS-HR (net CAGR >= 15% AND maxDD <= 60%, both windows)
nodes.norm_label: pass-hr (net cagr >= 15% and maxdd <= 60%, both windows)

nodes.label: PASS-RA (gate Sharpe >= 0.80, > benchmark both windows, +CAGR both)
nodes.norm_label: pass-ra (gate sharpe >= 0.80, > benchmark both windows, +cagr both)

nodes.label: Frozen-Regression Tripwire
nodes.rationale: 12 deterministic reference numbers pinned to exact values (d = +/-0.0000pp) so a silent drift from an 'unrelated' change fails loud. Has stayed GREEN across all 37 attempts.

nodes.label: swing_bot engine (prices, universe, coverage_gate, signals, backtest, rotation)
nodes.norm_label: swing_bot engine (prices, universe, coverage_gate, signals, backtest, rotation)

nodes.label: Execution/Signal Decomposition Ladder (Rung A/B/C)
nodes.rationale: Rung A frictionless close-to-close, Rung B next-open 0 bps, Rung C next-open + tiered cost — isolates whether a nominal edge is signal-real, gap-dwelling, or cost-gated (the EX-DECOMP method).

nodes.label: Mandatory Liquidity Floor (ADV >= $5M AND price >= $5)
nodes.rationale: At $100-1,000 of capital spread and slippage dominate, so the floor is non-optional — and it excludes exactly the small, illiquid, hard-to-borrow names where anomaly alpha concentrates.

nodes.label: Modified-Window Cap (verdict capped at PROMISING)
nodes.rationale: Data that cannot cover the hostile 2000-2013 gate (short interest 2018+, crypto ~2015+, SVXY 2011+) buys a structurally weaker test, so it may never claim PASS-HR/PASS-RA.

nodes.label: Append-Only Project Record (ground truth)
nodes.rationale: Prior entries are never edited; corrections are appended — so dead ends, a mis-scoped cost model, and one over-enthusiastic finding later corrected all remain visible instead of being tidied away.

nodes.label: Terminal Claim (no robust retail-EOD swing edge in the tested space)
nodes.rationale: Bounded by what was tested: the honest statement is 'no edge found in what was tested,' not 'no edge exists' — though what was tested now spans every free, EOD-testable mechanism family the program could identify.
nodes.norm_label: terminal claim (no robust retail-eod swing edge in the tested space)

nodes.label: Terminal Finding — decorrelation is not the scarce resource, EDGE is
nodes.rationale: The final three attempts each cleared the <=0.30 correlation bar comfortably (GLD +0.089, TLT -0.191, pairs -0.057) and each failed profitability: an uncorrelated return stream is trivial to find at retail scale, one whose edge survives retail costs is not.
nodes.norm_label: terminal finding — decorrelation is not the scarce resource, edge is

nodes.label: In-Sample-Composed Cap
nodes.rationale: A design composed after seeing prior results (M10-1, after 31) and that buys known survivors in crashes is a forward-paper hypothesis, not a live edge — the one design that actually CLEARED PASS-HR was still refused as a win.

nodes.label: M3 Forward Paper (Alpaca paper, live 2026-07-15)
nodes.rationale: The only lever producing uncontaminated (non-survivorship, non-in-sample) evidence; needs elapsed time rather than another attempt. Disclosed limitation: the three sleeves are ~one strategy — m10 runs the identical e6 rule on 69.7% of 4,226 sessions.

nodes.label: Overnight Gap (executioner #1)
nodes.rationale: The IBS/mean-reversion family loses >1/2 its edge to the overnight gap that a next-open EOD fill cannot capture (~54% component); only an intraday/MOC fill would capture it, and that is blocked by the EOD-only hard rule.

nodes.label: Turnover Cost (executioner #2)
nodes.rationale: Independently sinks what the gap leaves: ~93% of anomaly alpha dies under costs (Chen-Velikov), observed in-repo — only 1 of 5 decomposed FAILs was truly signal-dead.

nodes.label: 39-Name Survivor Large-Cap Universe
nodes.rationale: Deliberately biased in the strategy's favor to make FAILs decisive; M11 showed the bias is not merely a flattering tilt — the survivor set destroyed the documented bearish pattern edge by removing exactly the names a bearish pattern predicts.

nodes.label: E3 — Single-stock momentum (FAIL)
nodes.rationale: 6.27% gate CAGR, underperformed equal-weight buy-hold of its own survivor universe.

nodes.label: E6 — De-leveraged 1x moving-average trend rotation
nodes.rationale: PASS then downgraded: robust in the US but market-dependent (3/5 regions), cuts an 83% drawdown to ~52% at roughly market-level return — a drawdown-control overlay, explicitly NOT the high-return goal.

nodes.label: E8 — Volatility squeeze (FAIL)
nodes.rationale: Compression predicts expansion, not direction (gate CAGR -1.43%).

nodes.label: E11 — Volume-gated breakout (FAIL)
nodes.rationale: Volume gating adds nothing to the breakout signal.

nodes.label: E16 — Raw weekly reversal
nodes.rationale: Gate CAGR 16.76% — the only experiment to clear the 15% return bar — but on a 65.9% drawdown plus survivorship; EX-DECOMP measured a -4.96 pp gap bleed.

nodes.label: E18 — VIX term-structure overlay (weak PASS-RA)
nodes.rationale: The program's only PASS-RA and it is weak; gate is VIX/VIX3M < 1 (contango). A forward-paper candidate, not a live claim.

nodes.label: X1 — Volatility gate vs plain 200-DMA (FAIL)
nodes.rationale: Confirms no vol gate beats the plain 200-DMA.

nodes.label: X2/X2b — Short-interest days-to-cover anomaly
nodes.rationale: Real and correctly signed (+18.4% / Sharpe 0.98 frictionless) but structurally uncapturable: properly costed it collapses to 9.2% / 0.56 at 5% borrow, the pure short is negative at every borrow level, and it requires shorting — impossible at $100-1,000 with no fractional shorting. X2's initial write-up over-weighted the frictionless number; X2b corrected it and the record preserves both.

nodes.label: X6 — Crypto BTC/ETH dual-MA trend pilot (FAIL)
nodes.rationale: Crushes HODL in the 2018-22 bears (29.6% vs 4.3%, DD 82%->61%) but loses HODL's Sharpe in the 2023+ bull (0.76 < 1.01) — reproduces E6's lesson in a new domain: trend is drawdown control, not a return enhancer over buy-and-hold.
nodes.norm_label: x6 — crypto btc/eth dual-ma trend pilot (fail)

nodes.label: X7 — HYG:IEF credit-regime gate (FAIL)
nodes.rationale: The first gate ever to BEAT the plain 200-DMA in a window (GFC gate Sharpe 0.98 vs 0.61 — credit led 2008, so it de-risked earlier), then collapses in the 2014+ bull (3.81% / DD 47.6% / Sh 0.34, 221 whipsaw switches). A crisis specialist that self-destructs in bulls.

nodes.label: X8 — Non-equity trend on GLD/TLT (FAIL both arms)
nodes.rationale: Judged on an explicitly-labelled DIVERSIFIER bar declared before results. GLD is a 3-of-4 near-miss (Sharpe beat buy-hold in GATE, lost in SEC — the 6th one-window death); TLT's negative CAGR is materially understated by dividend-UNADJUSTED prices, a declared bias.
nodes.norm_label: x8 — non-equity trend on gld/tlt (fail both arms)

nodes.label: X9 — Gatev distance pairs / market-neutral relative value (FAIL)
nodes.rationale: The zero-cost diagnostic splits the failure: gross gate Sharpe 0.43, gross SEC -0.05 — the edge had already decayed BEFORE costs, then ~81 round trips/yr x ~20 bps ~= 16%/yr of drag finished it. 87.4% of trades converged: the mechanism works, the reversion is simply smaller than four legs of transaction cost.
nodes.norm_label: x9 — gatev distance pairs / market-neutral relative value (fail)

nodes.label: M10-1 Nagel Switch (in-sample-composed PASS-HR)
nodes.rationale: VIX>20 -> C1 residual reversal, VIX<=20 -> E6 trend. The program's FIRST PASS-HR (gate 17.87% / DD 59.95% / Sh 0.66) but composed after 31 results, survivor-flattered, DD clears by 0.05 pp, breaks at VIX>18 and at 15 bps, fails PASS-RA — forward-paper-only, not clean.

nodes.label: M10-2 — 2x QQQ stress mean-reversion (FAIL)
nodes.rationale: Gate 2.99% CAGR / 83.3% DD, and it closes the E2 'c2c mirage': the 5-day hold neutralized the overnight gap (c2c 3.18% ~= next-open 2.99%), proving the gap was hiding a falling 2x knife into 2000-02/2008, not alpha.

nodes.label: M11 — Chart-pattern geometry (FAIL, signal-dead)
nodes.rationale: Rule-based (NOT LLM) causal detection of long-side reversal shapes; the last untested classical mechanism, chosen because every other strategy trades a NUMBER and none trades SHAPE. Gate -0.14% CAGR / Sh 0.09 with frictionless Rung B ~= 0. Payload: the survivor universe destroyed the documented bearish pattern edge (fwd-20 +1.70% vs unconditional +1.15%, the opposite of Savin 2007).

nodes.author: Evan Daruwalla
nodes.rationale: PLAN ONLY, nothing run. Exists because the terminal claim is conditioned on constraints the program never tested for bindingness; a 2x2 isolates which constraint does the work.

nodes.label: M12 2x2 Controlled Factorial (Horizon x Concentration)
nodes.rationale: Reporting the two main effects plus the interaction is the entire point; running only the both-relaxed cell would have said nothing about WHICH relaxation mattered, which was the objection to 'both at once'.

nodes.label: Horizon factor H (10 vs 63 sessions)
nodes.rationale: Cost drag is the program's most repeated killer — X9 quantified it at ~16%/yr from ~81 round trips — and fewer, longer holds pay less toll.

nodes.label: Concentration factor K (3 vs 20)
nodes.rationale: The program's own Hou-Xue-Zhang explanation says a factor premium is a decile spread across many names that K=1-3 cannot express — this tests that assertion instead of continuing to assume it.

nodes.label: 12-1 cross-sectional momentum signal (t-252 to t-21)

nodes.label: momentum_v2 (Trading project, read-only reference)
nodes.rationale: Monthly horizon, K=50, VALIDATED (IS +21.0%/yr, OOS +26.5%/yr, OOS Sharpe 0.87) — the opposite-verdict endpoint to E3 in the same factor family.

nodes.label: OPEN universe decision (39 survivors / ~100 large-caps / Trading price_cache)
nodes.rationale: K=20 is only meaningful if the universe supports a real sort: top-20 of 39 is half the universe (tests direction, not magnitude). Recommended (b) ~100 large-caps — a genuine sort without coupling the two projects or inheriting price_cache's verified gaps (next_open 1.1M rows vs 15.7M close, only 3 delistings, median ticker 636 rows).
nodes.norm_label: open universe decision (39 survivors / ~100 large-caps / trading price_cache)

nodes.label: Diagnostic-not-deployment rule
nodes.rationale: Stated before any data is pulled because it is the easiest rule to break later: picking the best of four cells and deploying it IS in-sample composition — exactly the M10-1 mistake already capped. A winning cell requires a separate prereg on the D1 dual-bar before forward paper enters the conversation, and M12 cannot retroactively rewrite the search-phase terminal claim.

nodes.label: Pre-registration TEMPLATE
nodes.author: Evan Daruwalla
nodes.rationale: Standing template (M9 #43, record Appendix BT) binding every future prereg; [STANDING] sections are fixed policy that may not be weakened per-experiment, only filled in — an inapplicable rule must be disclosed with a dated reason, never silently dropped.

nodes.label: [STANDING] fixed-policy sections
nodes.rationale: Cannot be weakened per-experiment; only their blanks are filled. A standing rule that genuinely cannot apply must be named in Disclosed Limitations with a dated reason, never silently dropped.

nodes.label: Tiered cost model (1 / 5 / 15-25 bps per side + 15 bps stress leg)
nodes.rationale: 1 bp broad-index ETFs, 5 bps single stocks and sector ETFs, 15-25 bps or EXCLUDE below the liquidity floor, 25 bps crypto (Alpaca taker). The stress leg runs alongside the headline so cost-fragility is visible rather than discoverable later.
nodes.norm_label: tiered cost model (1 / 5 / 15-25 bps per side + 15 bps stress leg)

nodes.label: Time-stop baseline (price/trailing stops must BEAT it)
nodes.rationale: Stops interact with the overnight gap, so a naive stop is not free; any stop variant is an ADDITIONAL arm that must beat the time-stop-only arm to be adopted, and both are reported.
nodes.norm_label: time-stop baseline (price/trailing stops must beat it)

nodes.label: Probe-first data discipline
nodes.rationale: For any NEW data source, confirm fetch + parse + coverage BEFORE the prereg; if messy or thin, record BLOCKED-ON-DATA and stop (the E17/E19 pattern).

nodes.label: Sizing defaults (capped fractional-Kelly, anti-martingale, no leverage)
nodes.rationale: lambda <= 1/2 (never full Kelly) or fixed-risk r = 1-2% of NAV; never average down a loser; leverage only when the experiment IS a leverage test with a pre-committed regime stop. Frozen in the prereg because changing size rules after results is tuning.
nodes.norm_label: sizing defaults (capped fractional-kelly, anti-martingale, no leverage)

nodes.label: LLM overlays are forward-only
nodes.rationale: Any LLM-scored signal is a treatment arm on the M3 live-paper control and never a historical backtest — training-cutoff look-ahead makes LLM backtests dishonest.

nodes.label: Split-adjusted / dividend-UNADJUSTED convention (auto_adjust=False)
nodes.rationale: Every price consumer honors it and the runner header states it; the gap it leaves (no total-return path) is a declared bias, most visibly in TLT and SPY buy-hold comparisons.

nodes.label: Signal at close, execute next open (EOD hard rule)
nodes.rationale: No intraday logic until an intraday data source exists — which is also why the overnight-gap component the program repeatedly loses cannot be captured.
nodes.norm_label: signal at close, execute next open (eod hard rule)

nodes.label: Opportunistic vs Routine Insider-Trade Classification
nodes.rationale: A purchase in month m is ROUTINE if the same insider also bought in month m in each of the three prior years, else OPPORTUNISTIC; CMP found only pattern-breaking trades carry information (~82 bps/mo), so E19 trades only the opportunistic subset.

nodes.rationale: Entry uses the Form-4 filing date rather than the transaction date because the filing is what is publicly knowable at decision time (filed within 2 business days).

nodes.label: Dividend-Capture Ex-Date Accounting (D/P0 credit)
nodes.rationale: Because prices are dividend-UNADJUSTED, the ex-date drop would read as a pure loss unless the received dividend is credited to P&L; the per-trade return therefore adds a D/P0 term explicitly.

A-priori prior POOR (program base rate 0/8; breakout systems on liquid indices post-2000 historically weak). Long-only because the short side of US equities is structurally worse for a small account.

nodes.label: Never-Book-a-Loss Deep-Dip Strategy (buy ≤0.80×ATH, sell +15%, no stop)
nodes.rationale: Audit with pre-stated dual readout: (1) the 'never book a loss' property will be nearly true in realized terms — the seductive statistic; (2) NAV will still show large unrealized drawdown and CAGR well below 15% because capital idles, winners are capped, losers held uncapped. Either prediction failing is informative. ETFs used because a single-stock version is survivorship-poisoned (E3 lesson).

nodes.label: No Tuning a FAIL
nodes.rationale: Thresholds and parameters are fixed in the prereg before the run; a failing result is never re-tuned into a pass, and no post-hoc bolt-on de-risking is permitted.

nodes.label: VIX > 20 Regime Switch (STRESS vs CALM)

nodes.label: Purged K-Fold with Embargo (K=6, embargo 1%)
nodes.rationale: Labels built from forward windows leak into folds that touch those windows, so standard K-fold reports skill that does not exist; training observations overlapping a test label window are dropped, plus a 1% embargo after each test block.

nodes.label: CPCV (N=6 groups, 2 test groups, 15 combinations)
nodes.rationale: A single train/test split yields one path and one Sharpe - no distribution and no variance across paths; reporting the full distribution is mandatory because with concentrated books median and mean diverge sharply.

nodes.label: Deflated Sharpe Ratio (DSR)
nodes.rationale: Adjusts an observed Sharpe for trial count, skew/kurtosis, and sample length; a strategy-level test of whether the Sharpe survives the number of trials searched.

nodes.label: Probability of Backtest Overfitting (PBO via CSCV)
nodes.rationale: Selection-level test: the fraction of splits where the in-sample-best configuration underperforms the median OOS. PBO > 0.5 means the selection procedure is worse than random - it measures selection, not edge.
nodes.norm_label: probability of backtest overfitting (pbo via cscv)

nodes.label: Measured Round-Trip Friction Model
nodes.rationale: Friction is the signed gap between the price the simulation assumed and the price actually obtained, computed per fill from live paper fills - never an assumed constant. It ships uncalibrated: n=4 fills cannot estimate a distribution, so it is an instrument, not a number.

nodes.label: Fail-Loud on Missing Measurement (MIN_FILLS_FOR_ESTIMATE = 20)
nodes.rationale: estimate_friction() raises rather than falling back to a constant or a defaulted warning; a caller may proceed only by passing an explicit assumed_bps, which stamps friction_source=ASSUMED on every downstream artifact so no report can present an assumption as a measurement.

nodes.label: Trial Count as Hard Input (larger of the two figures)
nodes.rationale: Read from trial_log.json, raising if missing or older than the newest prereg, because a stale log under-counts trials in exactly the direction that flatters the result; the 37-vs-38 discrepancy is resolved by erring toward more trials, and the count must print in the same block as the DSR.
nodes.norm_label: trial count as hard input (larger of the two figures)

nodes.label: Planted-Edge Falsifier (reported, not gated)
nodes.rationale: A harness that rejects everything is as useless as one that accepts everything, so a synthetic series with a genuinely predictable feature is fed in and must NOT be rejected; otherwise criteria 1-2 are satisfied trivially and the rejections carry no information.

nodes.label: Success Condition: The Harness Must REJECT Things
nodes.rationale: A validation layer that passes noise is not merely weak, it is harmful - it manufactures false confidence in exactly the situation it exists to prevent, so rejection of a worthless signal is pre-registered as the acceptance test before any code is written.
nodes.norm_label: success condition: the harness must reject things

nodes.label: Prereg V2: Amended Harness Acceptance Criterion
nodes.norm_label: prereg v2: amended harness acceptance criterion

nodes.label: Amended OR-Rule: Rejected if DSR Insignificant OR PBO >= 0.5
nodes.rationale: V1's AND-conjunction was mis-specified: DSR is strategy-level and PBO is selection-level, so requiring both demanded one strategy fail two unrelated tests. A no-edge rule with highly correlated variants has almost no selection to overfit, so its PBO sits near random while DSR correctly says no edge. Both statistics are still reported separately.
nodes.norm_label: amended or-rule: rejected if dsr insignificant or pbo >= 0.5

nodes.label: Amend by Superseding, Never by Rewriting the Original
nodes.rationale: V1 failed its own criterion 2 and that failure stands on the record; amending a criterion by rewriting the document it lives in would erase the evidence that it was ever wrong, which is the entire reason the project pre-registers anything.
nodes.norm_label: amend by superseding, never by rewriting the original

nodes.label: Predicted False Positive: Planted Edge Rejected via PBO 0.514
nodes.rationale: Written down in advance rather than explained away afterwards. Pre-committed handling: report it as a stated limitation of the selection-level axis - PBO is only meaningful when the configuration set represents a genuine selection choice - and do NOT loosen PBO_FAIL_AT or drop the falsifier; a V3 would compute PBO only over real selection sets.
nodes.norm_label: predicted false positive: planted edge rejected via pbo 0.514

nodes.rationale: Measured: 54% of the close-to-close IBS edge lives in the close→next-open gap (6.3 of 11.8 bps pooled); next-open execution keeps ~64% of the edge because reversion continues into a second night. Many single-country ETFs' IBS edge is a stale-NAV/overnight artifact a next-open loop cannot harvest. This gap between 'the effect is real' and 'you can capture it at next open' became the story of the entire project.

nodes.label: E18 regime-gate bake-off
nodes.rationale: Four a-priori risk-on/off gates run as drawdown overlays on a 1x QQQ sleeve, next-open, 5 bps/side, vs QQQ buy-hold. Verdict: no new regime gate beats the plain 200-DMA overlay on the robust criterion — neither VIX term structure, credit spreads, nor breadth improves on trend-timing across regimes.

nodes.label: E18 VIX/VIX3M term-structure gate (weak PASS-RA)
nodes.rationale: The program's first PASS-RA and a fragile one. The 2006-13 gate window contains exactly ONE crash (2008) because VIX3M history starts 2006, so the arm misses the 2000-02 dot-com bear entirely — a gate that goes to cash on high near-term vol always looks good in a short sample dominated by the one event it dodged. It also FAILS its own overlay test in the other regime: 2014-> drawdown 44.1% vs buy-hold 35.6% (it whipsawed in the low-vol bull) and secondary Sharpe 0.79 barely edges SPY. Honest label: weak PASS-RA, forward-paper candidate only, never a return engine and never live capital.

nodes.label: E6 1x 200-DMA trend overlay
nodes.rationale: The only gate satisfying the overlay criteria in BOTH windows, confirming E6/E7: plain trend-timing is the robust drawdown overlay and the one deployable artifact the program has produced.

nodes.label: HY-OAS credit-spread gate — INCONCLUSIVE (data)
nodes.rationale: Not a FAIL but a data hole: the free FRED fredgraph.csv endpoint returned BAMLH0A0HYM2 only from ~2023-07 despite a cosd=1996 request, leaving no gate- or secondary-window history to test. A working FRED fetch (API key or corrected endpoint) would unblock it; not pursued.

nodes.label: Breadth >= 50% gate
nodes.rationale: Meets the overlay criterion in the 2000-13 gate window only (0.96% CAGR at 65.6% maxDD) and fails it in the secondary window — one-window survival, the recurring shape of every gate except plain trend.

nodes.label: Robust overlay criterion (maxDD cut >= 10pp AND Sharpe >= buy-hold in BOTH windows)
nodes.rationale: The pre-registered two-window robustness bar that converts 'looked good once' into 'holds across regimes'; it is what disqualifies the VIX-TS, breadth and HY-OAS arms while passing plain 200-DMA.
nodes.norm_label: robust overlay criterion (maxdd cut >= 10pp and sharpe >= buy-hold in both windows)

nodes.label: D1 dual-bar verdict scheme (PASS-HR / PASS-RA)
nodes.rationale: PASS-HR = CAGR >= 15% with maxDD <= 60% in both windows; PASS-RA = gate Sharpe >= 0.80 AND above buy-hold in both windows AND positive CAGR in both. A PASS-RA becomes an M3 forward-paper candidate and does NOT authorize live capital. All outcomes fixed before running.

nodes.label: VIX3M 2006 history floor
nodes.rationale: VIX3M only exists from 2006-07-17, truncating the VIX-TS gate window to 2006-13 and excluding the 2000-02 bear. Disclosed in the prereg; it is the single fact that makes the E18 pass fragile.

nodes.label: Program tally — 1 weak PASS-RA / 18 attempts, PASS-HR column 0
nodes.rationale: The running falsification ledger; it is the base rate every later effort/no-effort decision is priced against.
nodes.norm_label: program tally — 1 weak pass-ra / 18 attempts, pass-hr column 0

nodes.rationale: JPM has 25,342 total filings; reaching the 2000-2013 window requires paginating EDGAR's older submission archives or the quarterly full-index — tens of thousands of raw-XML fetches across 39 names under a 10 req/s limit.

nodes.label: Effort-vs-base-rate deferral
nodes.rationale: Full gate-window ingestion is the heaviest build the project would attempt (hours, tens of thousands of fetches, plus CIK-history and raw-XML hazards), and E19 inherits E3's survivorship so only a FAIL is clean. Against a base rate of 0 PASS-HR / 19 attempts, spending that effort for a near-certain interpretable-FAIL is a poor trade to make autonomously.

nodes.label: Asymmetric-falsification doctrine (survivor universe: only a FAIL is clean)
nodes.rationale: On a survivor universe every bias runs in the strategy's favour, so a FAIL is the strongest negative available and any PASS is uninterpretable and routes to forward paper rather than being claimed.
nodes.norm_label: asymmetric-falsification doctrine (survivor universe: only a fail is clean)

nodes.label: 39-stock survivor large-cap universe

nodes.label: Cohen, Malloy & Pomorski (2012) — Decoding Inside Information
nodes.rationale: Opportunistic (pattern-breaking) insider buys ~82 bps/mo value-weighted abnormal returns, routine trades nothing; effect strongest in small caps — exactly the names a mandatory liquidity floor excludes.

nodes.label: E20 dividend capture — FAIL
nodes.rationale: Buy close before ex-date, sell ex-date open, credit the dividend; 29 ETFs, 2,345 capture trades, 5 bps/side. FAIL on both D1 tiers (gate 0.62% CAGR / Sharpe 0.18; secondary -1.15% / -0.39).

nodes.label: Ex-date price-drop deficiency (real but sub-scale)
nodes.rationale: The ex-date drop averages ~10 bps LESS than the dividend net of costs — a genuine per-trade edge (+0.10%/trade, 57.7% win rate). It fails not on sign but on scale: ~90 captures/yr of one session each means the edge barely touches the capital, compounding to 0.62%/yr in the gate window.

nodes.label: Ordinary-income dividend tax flips the gross edge negative
nodes.rationale: All figures are pre-tax; dividends are taxed as ordinary income, which (disclosed in the prereg before the run) would flip the +0.10%/trade gross edge negative for a real retail account. The folklore edge exists, is tiny, decayed, and is eaten by tax.
nodes.norm_label: ordinary-income dividend tax flips the gross edge negative

nodes.label: Post-2014 decay of the capture edge
nodes.rationale: Gate 0.62%/yr turns to -1.15%/yr after 2014 — another micro-effect that decayed, matching the McLean-Pontiff post-publication pattern seen across the program.
nodes.norm_label: post-2014 decay of the capture edge

nodes.label: Dividend-UNadjusted price convention
nodes.rationale: Split-adjusted / dividend-UNadjusted closes are exactly the convention needed to measure the ex-date drop; the standing data convention finally works FOR a test instead of against it.

nodes.label: E13 turn-of-the-month overlay — FAIL
nodes.rationale: Long SPY on turn-of-month days (last session + first 3), cash otherwise; in-market 19.1% of sessions, 403 round-trips. FAIL on both tiers: 1.4%/yr vs the 15% bar, gate Sharpe 0.20, and crushed in 2014-> (0.23 vs SPY 0.74) where PASS-RA requires beating SPY in BOTH windows.

nodes.label: Month-turn return concentration (real, but a risk-reduction observation)
nodes.rationale: In the sideways/bear 2000-2013 decade TOM matched SPY's return (1.41% vs 1.72%) while holding cash 81% of the time — a genuine demonstration of the McConnell-Xu concentration effect. But that is risk reduction, not edge: in the 2014-> bull, sitting in cash 81% of the time forfeited the trend and lost decisively. Real-but-small and regime-dependent.
nodes.norm_label: month-turn return concentration (real, but a risk-reduction observation)

nodes.label: McConnell & Xu (2008) — Equity Returns at the Turn of the Month
nodes.rationale: ~15 bps/day over a 4-day window; peer-reviewed, and killed locally by E13.
nodes.norm_label: mcconnell & xu (2008) — equity returns at the turn of the month

nodes.label: E14 diversified sector momentum — FAIL
nodes.rationale: Top-3 of 11 SPDR sectors by trailing 126-session return, 21-session rebalance, 969 entries. FAIL on both tiers (2.42% gate CAGR, Sharpe 0.22).

nodes.label: Equal-weight 11-sector null (EW-11)
nodes.rationale: The honest benchmark that turns 'low return' into 'negative alpha': momentum selection lost to passively equal-weighting the SAME sectors in every window (gate 2.42% vs 4.13%; secondary 6.99% vs 10.53%).

nodes.label: Survivorship-clean design
nodes.rationale: All 11 sectors exist with no delisting bias, so unlike E3 this result needs no asymmetric 'only-a-FAIL-is-clean' framing and is fully interpretable in both directions — the program's cleanest FAIL to date, on data that could not have been rigged.

nodes.label: Momentum selection destroyed value vs passive equal weight
nodes.rationale: Chasing the top-3 trailing-6-month sectors underperformed just holding all of them — an unbiased confirmation that concentrated momentum, the single most-cited retail edge, does not survive at this horizon net of cost.
nodes.norm_label: momentum selection destroyed value vs passive equal weight

nodes.label: Data-type exploration brief (beyond daily OHLCV)
nodes.author: Evan Daruwalla
nodes.rationale: Every availability claim probed live 2026-07-12 rather than assumed. Six new data types are genuinely free, three hard-blocked, and the available ones skew heavily toward regime gates and overlays, not return engines — the same shape as the OHLCV conclusion. Feeds the E18/E19/E20 additions to M7.

nodes.label: VIX complex availability (VIX 1990, VIX3M 2006, VVIX/SKEW)
nodes.rationale: Probed: ^VIX 1990-01-02-> (9,198 bars), ^VIX3M 2006-07-17->, VIX9D 2011+, VVIX 2007+, SKEW 1990+. The VIX3M start date is what caps the E18 gate window and makes its pass fragile.

nodes.label: Self-computed market breadth
nodes.rationale: % above 200DMA and A/D computable from the project's own 107 cached series — zero new data risk. But the base is 29 ETFs + 39 survivor stocks, not the NYSE tape the folklore is built on, so it is a cheap regime FEATURE, not an experiment worth its own prereg.

nodes.label: Zweig Breadth Thrust
nodes.rationale: Practitioner-sourced claim (+20% avg 12mo after a signal) resting on N < 30 signals since 1950 — statistically fragile and position-horizon, so any test here is INCONCLUSIVE-prone by construction.

nodes.label: FRED keyless fredgraph.csv feed
nodes.rationale: T10Y2Y 1976->, ICSA 1967->, BAMLH0A0HYM2 endpoint works but the default window is ~3yr and the full 1996-> series needs a cosd date param — the exact detail that later left E18's HY-OAS arm INCONCLUSIVE. Publication-lag/revision nuance means ALFRED vintages exist for honesty.

nodes.label: BLOCKED-AT-$0 data boundary
nodes.rationale: Recorded so nobody re-litigates: options chains/IV history (current chains only, no history), short-interest history (E17's FINRA probe), historical news sentiment (no free point-in-time archive -> forward-only), Google Trends (resampled/renormalized per request -> irreproducible backtests, rejected on rigor grounds), 13F (45-day lag -> position trading), crypto (a new asset class, not a data type).

nodes.label: Available data types buy overlays, not return engines
nodes.rationale: Both standout candidates (VIX term structure, FRED macro/credit) defend drawdown rather than add return, and the E6/E7 arc already showed how such gates fail to add return. Only EDGAR Form 4 had a real shot at a return edge.
nodes.norm_label: available data types buy overlays, not return engines

nodes.label: probe_datatypes.py
nodes.rationale: Run 2026-07-12 against yfinance + FRED endpoints; the source of every availability fact in the brief.

nodes.label: Full swing-method survey (~90 methods, 8 families)
nodes.author: Evan Daruwalla
nodes.rationale: Eight parallel desk-research agents, one per family, each grading evidence tier and issuing a testability verdict, plus a reconciliation layer added at compile that cross-checked every 'genuinely untested' claim against the project's own E1-E20 ledger. Desk research only — no backtests were run, so every testability verdict is a scoping judgment, not a result.

nodes.label: H0 survives — the residual search space is exhausted of high-return retail-EOD engines
nodes.rationale: H1 ('a method with real merit exists that the project simply hasn't tried') is rejected in its strong form: the untried methods are refinements of local kills, overlays, or carry published strong-FAIL priors. What remains are risk-adjusted overlays and honest kill-shots — consistent with the program reaching its autonomous wall.
nodes.norm_label: h0 survives — the residual search space is exhausted of high-return retail-eod engines

nodes.label: Family-vs-ledger reconciliation table
nodes.rationale: The load-bearing table mapping each literature family to the experiment that already probed it here, so 'merit in the literature' is never confused with 'open for this project'. It reclassified several top-line candidates from open to already-killed. Representatives of every family except chart-pattern TA and factor/ML have been directly tested and every one failed the high-return bar — and those two untested families carry the WORST priors.

nodes.label: Concentration destroys the edge (K=1-3 keeps the mean, adds back the variance)
nodes.rationale: Nearly every method with peer-reviewed merit is a diversified long-short decile premium. Collapsing one to K=1-3 liquid names discards the diversification that IS the edge and keeps only the shrunken, decayed, cost-eroded mean plus idiosyncratic noise — a structural void, not a tuning problem.
nodes.norm_label: concentration destroys the edge (k=1-3 keeps the mean, adds back the variance)

nodes.label: The edge lives where you can't trade (microcap / illiquid / distressed)
nodes.rationale: Reversal, short interest, ML, Baker-Wurgler and PEAD all concentrate alpha in exactly the names the mandatory liquidity floor excludes; 65-82% of 452 anomalies fail once value-weighted with microcaps dropped.
nodes.norm_label: the edge lives where you can't trade (microcap / illiquid / distressed)

nodes.label: Mandatory liquidity floor (ADV >= $5M AND price >= $5)
nodes.rationale: Non-negotiable at this capital size because spread/slippage dominate — and it is simultaneously the single biggest reason documented anomalies cannot be harvested here, since their alpha concentrates in the excluded names.

nodes.label: Ranked shortlist of 7 genuinely-open ideas
nodes.rationale: Long-only-capable, EOD-codifiable, free-data, not yet falsified here: residual reversal, dividend-initiation drift, one consolidated volatility-breakout kill-shot, vol-targeting sizing overlay, Reg SHO short-volume drift, even-week FOMC overlay, SVXY short-vol carry. ALL carry a strong prior of missing the 15% bar.

nodes.label: Short-term residual reversal (shortlist #1)
nodes.rationale: Strips the factor betas that drove E16's 65.9% drawdown, so it is the logical refinement after raw weekly reversal. Honest caveat: Nagel shows reversal returns ARE close-anchored liquidity provision, so next-open execution bleeds the same gap that killed the oscillator cluster; and it needs a diversified book, which fights K=1-3.

nodes.label: One consolidated volatility-breakout kill-shot (shortlist #3)
nodes.rationale: Donchian ~ Bollinger-squeeze ~ ATR ~ Keltner collapsed into ONE pre-registered spec specifically to avoid multiple testing. Its merit lives in futures; on single equities under 5 bps and next-open the Sullivan-Timmermann-White / Bajgrowicz / Marshall trilogy predicts it dies — so it is entered as an honest kill-shot, not a candidate.

nodes.label: Hou, Xue & Zhang (2020) — Replicating Anomalies
nodes.rationale: 65-82% of 452 anomalies fail once you value-weight and drop microcaps.

nodes.label: E19 opportunistic insider-buy drift — FAIL (clean, robust to cleaning)
nodes.author: Evan Daruwalla
nodes.rationale: Form-4 opportunistic buys, next-open entry, 40-session hold, K=5 on the 39-name survivor universe produce a SUB-BETA long-only sleeve: gate 4.68%/0.31 and secondary 4.91%/0.35, underperforming SPY on CAGR and Sharpe in BOTH windows. Both pre-registered tiers fail. Asymmetric close: survivorship could only help and contamination could only mask, and the sensitivity ruled masking out — so the FAIL is clean in both directions.
nodes.norm_label: e19 opportunistic insider-buy drift — fail (clean, robust to cleaning)

nodes.label: CMP routine-vs-opportunistic classifier
nodes.rationale: Routine = the reporting owner bought in the same calendar month in each of the prior 3 years; everything else is opportunistic. It passed 6,138 of 6,435 P-buys (95%) through as opportunistic, FALSIFYING the Appendix-BQ prediction that the same-month-3-years rule would absorb DRIP traffic as routine — DRIP cadence and duplicate line-items don't map onto a same-month-each-year pattern, so they leak through.

nodes.label: transactionCode-P contamination
nodes.rationale: The per-ticker P-buy distribution is pathological: BAC alone is 2,851 of 6,435 P-buys (44%), dominated by owner CIK 0000070858 which is Bank of America's OWN ISSUER CIK, not an insider, and includes 1-share lots priced $0.01-0.02 — physically impossible as real open-market purchases (DRIP/fractional/accounting artifacts mis-coded as 'P').

nodes.label: Contamination is bidirectional, not only inflationary
nodes.rationale: Corrects Appendix BQ's claim that contamination 'can only inflate a spurious PASS'. Mechanical signal-free buys pull the sleeve toward market beta, which could equally MASK a real edge by diluting it — the genuine threat to a FAIL, and the reason a sensitivity was required before closing.
nodes.norm_label: contamination is bidirectional, not only inflationary

nodes.label: Post-hoc de-junk sensitivity
nodes.rationale: Price floors ($1/$5) plus same-owner-same-day dedup cut entries 6,119 -> 2,675, yet every variant stays flat and sub-beta (gate Sharpe 0.27-0.31). Per doctrine a pass here would have been 'PROMISING / needs a fresh prereg', never a claimed PASS — none flipped, so cleaning does not reveal a masked edge.

nodes.label: K=5 / 40-session book saturation
nodes.rationale: Gate entries used stay at ~279 across every filter variant because a K=5 book holding 40 sessions saturates — THROUGHPUT, not raw signal count, sets the trade rate. Explains why halving the signal set changed nothing.

nodes.label: Diversified anomaly collapses to a sub-beta long-only book
nodes.rationale: The documented insider-buy alpha lives in small, illiquid names the liquidity floor excludes, and next-open EOD execution surrenders any announcement pop. The survivor large-caps (all of which did fine long-term) give the sleeve market beta and nothing more.
nodes.norm_label: diversified anomaly collapses to a sub-beta long-only book

nodes.label: Lakonishok & Lee (2001) — Are Insiders' Trades Informative?
nodes.rationale: Insider-buy informativeness concentrated in small firms — the same liquidity wall that neutralised E19.
nodes.norm_label: lakonishok & lee (2001) — are insiders' trades informative?

nodes.label: EX-DECOMP — execution/signal decomposition of five closed FAILs
nodes.author: Evan Daruwalla
nodes.rationale: Diagnostic, no D1 verdict and no tuning. The PRD expected 'most land SIGNAL-DEAD' — that is WRONG; only E14 is signal-dead. The others carry real gross structure that dies for different, now-named reasons, so the program's failures are heterogeneous rather than one flat 'no signal'. Zero execution-logic edits: Rung A is obtained by wrapping the price feed so each bar's open := prior close.
nodes.norm_label: ex-decomp — execution/signal decomposition of five closed fails

nodes.label: Three-rung execution ladder (A c2c 0bps / B next-open 0bps / C next-open +5bps)
nodes.rationale: A->B isolates the overnight gap; B->C isolates the cost/turnover drag. Benchmarks read closes so they are identical across rungs, which is what makes the deltas attributable.
nodes.norm_label: three-rung execution ladder (a c2c 0bps / b next-open 0bps / c next-open +5bps)

nodes.label: SIGNAL-DEAD class
nodes.rationale: A <= null: no alpha to execute, cost irrelevant. Only E14 lands here — even frictionless close-to-close (4.06%) it does not beat equal-weighting the same sectors (4.13%).

nodes.label: COST-GATED class
nodes.rationale: Beats the null at B, dies B->C. E13 is the case: frictionless 3.40% vs SPY 1.72% and still 2.64% at next-open, with the 5 bps/side turnover cost (-1.23 pp) dragging it to the recorded 1.41%. A real gross calendar edge killed by cost — not 'matched SPY by luck'.

nodes.label: SURVIVES-NULL class
nodes.rationale: Still beats the null at Rung C, so the D1 FAIL is about the 15% bar and the DD ceiling, not the signal. E15 and E16 land here in the gate window — but SURVIVES-NULL means 'beats the passive basket', never 'passes D1', and both fall below their null post-2014.

nodes.label: GAP-DWELLER class
nodes.rationale: Beats the null at A and dies A->B — the edge lived entirely in the close-to-open move a next-open fill cannot reach. No closed FAIL in this batch landed here, which is itself the finding.

nodes.label: Two recurring killers — the overnight gap and cost/turnover
nodes.rationale: Each independently sinks edges and which dominates depends on holding period and direction: momentum/timing (E13, E16) LOSE to the gap, while mean-reversion/event overnight trades (E15, E20) GAIN from it and then pay it back in cost. Cost scales with turnover and is decisive — E16 weekly rebalance -6.25 pp, E20 2x5 bps/overnight-trade -10 bps — the Chen-Velikov mechanism observed directly in-repo.
nodes.norm_label: two recurring killers — the overnight gap and cost/turnover

nodes.label: E20's ex-date edge is gap-loaded
nodes.rationale: B (close->open, +34.5 bps) far exceeds A (close->close, +16.9 bps): by the close the ex-date price deficiency has largely mean-reverted away, so the effect is an OVERNIGHT one. It survives cost in the gate (+24.5 bps/trade) but is too small to compound and goes negative after cost post-2014 (-5.0 bps).

nodes.label: E16's gate SURVIVES-NULL is a survivorship artifact
nodes.rationale: Buying the biggest 5-day losers on a SURVIVOR universe systematically buys dips in names already known to have recovered; the decomposition cannot launder that. The tell is post-2014, where Rung C 10.68% falls BELOW EW-univ 13.97% — once the survivorship tailwind weakens, dip-selection loses to just holding the basket.
nodes.norm_label: e16's gate survives-null is a survivorship artifact

nodes.label: Rung-C regression gate
nodes.rationale: Rung C must reproduce the recorded numbers before any decomposition is believed (E13 gate 1.41% vs rec 1.40%; E16 16.76% exact; E20 +9.2 bps ~ recorded +0.10%/trade). GREEN — this is what separates a diagnostic from a re-run with different answers.

nodes.label: Chen & Velikov (2023) — Zeroing In on the Expected Returns of Anomalies
nodes.rationale: 204 anomalies decay ~50% out-of-sample and ~93% net of costs; the average anomaly nets ~4 bps/month. The literature base rate that makes 0-for-20 the EXPECTED output of honest research.
nodes.norm_label: chen & velikov (2023) — zeroing in on the expected returns of anomalies

nodes.label: X1 conditional volatility targeting (E6 x E18) — FAIL
nodes.author: Evan Daruwalla
nodes.rationale: H1 rejected, null survives. In the 2006-2013 gate the plain E6 200-DMA arm is the BEST risk manager (Sharpe 0.58, maxDD 19.9% vs SPY 0.32 / 56.5%); the conditional arm ties the VIX-TS arm at 0.42 and loses to E6, failing the pre-registered PASS-RA bar.
nodes.norm_label: x1 conditional volatility targeting (e6 x e18) — fail

nodes.label: Conditional de-risk rule (vol elevated AND trend broken)
nodes.rationale: Why it fails its own hypothesis: requiring BOTH conditions keeps the sleeve invested 88.7% of the time versus E6's 70%, so it barely de-risks and its drawdown (37.3%) sits near buy-hold rather than near E6. The 'stay invested when vol spikes inside an uptrend' intuition is real, but the binding drawdowns (2008) are exactly when trend IS broken, so the extra condition mostly just removes E6's protective exits during choppy-but-down-trending stretches.
nodes.norm_label: conditional de-risk rule (vol elevated and trend broken)

nodes.label: Cost stress 1/5/15 bps — cost is not the failure mechanism
nodes.rationale: Gate Sharpe 0.42 -> 0.39 -> 0.32 across 1/5/15 bps. Cost-robust, which rules out the usual killer and isolates the design flaw as the cause.
nodes.norm_label: cost stress 1/5/15 bps — cost is not the failure mechanism

nodes.label: Low effective N — one gate window is essentially one crash
nodes.rationale: Pre-registered as descriptive for this reason: a directional read, not a validated edge. Also SPY-only (E7 showed 200-DMA overlays are market-dependent) and the gate is 2006-2013 rather than the full hostile 2000-2013 window.
nodes.norm_label: low effective n — one gate window is essentially one crash

nodes.label: X2 days-to-cover / short-interest drift — FAIL (deployable long-only leg)
nodes.author: Evan Daruwalla
nodes.rationale: A clean falsification of the TRADEABLE idea and a validation of the a-priori reasoning: the prereg predicted in advance that the long-only leg tests the weak side and the alpha sits on the non-deployable short leg, and that is exactly what happened.
nodes.norm_label: x2 days-to-cover / short-interest drift — fail (deployable long-only leg)

nodes.label: Deployable long-only low-DTC leg
nodes.rationale: 13.32% CAGR beats SPY (12.53%) and EW-39 (9.59%) on raw CAGR but LOSES Sharpe to SPY (0.60 < 0.71) with a 35% drawdown in a mostly-bull decade, failing the pre-registered 'CAGR AND Sharpe vs both' bar. Decomposition: A->B is flat (16.07 vs 15.93) so this is NOT a gap-dwelling edge — the erosion is pure cost (B->C -2.75 pp from biweekly turnover), and even gross the long side barely matches SPY.

nodes.label: Long-short existence spread (+18.39% CAGR, Sharpe 0.98)
nodes.rationale: Decomposes exactly as theory predicts: low-DTC +15.77% vs high-DTC -2.63%, i.e. the most-shorted mega-caps underperformed SPY by ~15 pp/yr. The alpha is ENTIRELY on the short/high-DTC leg, which is not deployable at $100-1,000 (no fractional shorting, borrow). Existence-confirmed, non-deployable — not counted toward PASS-HR. Later corrected by X2b as too generous.

nodes.label: Survivorship makes the short-leg result a LOWER bound
nodes.rationale: The universe excludes names that were heavily shorted and then delisted/crashed — the short seller's biggest wins — so the true short-side alpha is if anything larger than the measured -2.63%. Here survivorship cuts AGAINST the finding and therefore strengthens it, the reverse of the usual direction.
nodes.norm_label: survivorship makes the short-leg result a lower bound

nodes.label: MODIFIED-WINDOW CAP (single window -> best achievable is PROMISING)
nodes.rationale: A single 2018-2026 window (one covid crash, one 2022 bear) caps the achievable verdict below PASS-HR/PASS-RA before the run. The deployable leg did not even reach the capped bar, so window thinness is not load-bearing for the FAIL.
nodes.norm_label: modified-window cap (single window -> best achievable is promising)

nodes.label: Lookahead guard — enter 10 sessions after the settlement date
nodes.rationale: FINRA short interest is settlement-dated but disseminated ~8-9 business days later; entering 10 trading sessions after settlement puts the signal strictly after it was public.
nodes.norm_label: lookahead guard — enter 10 sessions after the settlement date

nodes.label: FINRA consolidated short-interest REST API
nodes.rationale: Public, no auth; 205 biweekly settlement dates 2017-12-29 -> 2026-06-30 at 39/39 coverage with daysToCoverQuantity precomputed. Free exchange-listed consolidated SI exists only from June 2021 (pre-2021 free SI is OTC-only), which is the E17 'wall' and the reason X2 runs a modern-OOS window.

nodes.label: Asquith, Pathak & Ritter (2005) — Short Interest, Institutional Ownership, and Stock Returns
nodes.norm_label: asquith, pathak & ritter (2005) — short interest, institutional ownership, and stock returns

nodes.label: Boehmer, Huszar & Jordan (2010) — The Good News in Short Interest
nodes.norm_label: boehmer, huszar & jordan (2010) — the good news in short interest

nodes.label: X2b short-side / long-short DTC, borrow-costed — FAIL
nodes.author: Evan Daruwalla
nodes.rationale: Properly costed, the dollar-neutral long-short decays from a frictionless 17.13% / Sharpe 0.92 to 9.24% / Sharpe 0.56 at a realistic 5% borrow, and it is lumpy. Against the pre-registered market-neutral bar it is a clean FAIL — even the most generous 0%-borrow case (Sharpe 0.82) fails the robustness leg. The short-side lead is closed and the pivot away from the high-return-long goal is not worth making.
nodes.norm_label: x2b short-side / long-short dtc, borrow-costed — fail

nodes.label: Borrow-fee sweep 0/2/5/10/20% and the 13.8% breakeven
nodes.rationale: Real per-name cost-to-borrow is paid data (Ortex, Evan-gated), so it is SWEPT rather than measured. Breakeven borrow is 13.8%/yr, far above the ~0.3-3% general-collateral borrow these liquid mega-caps actually carry — so, unlike the Muravyev-Pearson-Pollet borrow-fee story that bites in illiquid names, borrow is NOT the killer here and paid borrow data would not rescue the result.

nodes.label: Lumpiness — only 5 of 9 calendar years positive
nodes.rationale: At 5% borrow: 2019/2023/2025/2026 carry the whole result while 2018/2021/2022/2024 lose. 55% positive years fails the pre-registered >= 70% robustness leg, which is what makes this a FAIL on risk-adjusted return and concentration rather than on cost.
nodes.norm_label: lumpiness — only 5 of 9 calendar years positive

nodes.label: Pure short of high-DTC mega-caps loses at every borrow level
nodes.rationale: -2.10% even at ZERO borrow. The 'most-shorted' basket is a MIX — IBM +7.2%, TXN +17.8%, ORCL +23.7% annualized while held — so being heavily shorted did not make them fall; add volatility drag (shorting volatile names compounds against you even when they end roughly flat) and a bull tape, and the short leg is a loser. The long-short only works gross because the LONG low-DTC leg carries it, hedged to market-neutral.
nodes.norm_label: pure short of high-dtc mega-caps loses at every borrow level

nodes.label: Delta-turnover trading model (continuers keep their shares)
nodes.rationale: The first cut of the runner over-charged by churning the whole book each cycle; charging 5 bps/side on delta turnover only is the fair model. A cost-model bug that would have manufactured a fake FAIL, caught and fixed.
nodes.norm_label: delta-turnover trading model (continuers keep their shares)

nodes.label: Correction of X2's headline
nodes.rationale: Calling the spread 'the program's strongest real anomaly' over-weighted a zero-cost, zero-borrow number. Properly costed and robustness-tested it is a FAIL — a lumpy market-neutral factor clearing no deployable bar. Better to learn that from a $0 borrow sweep than after funding an Ortex subscription and a margin account.

nodes.label: Market-neutral bar (Sharpe >= 0.80 + positive CAGR + >= 70% positive years at 5% borrow)
nodes.rationale: SPY is the wrong benchmark for a dollar-neutral sleeve, so the prereg swapped in an absolute market-neutral bar with an explicit robustness leg.
nodes.norm_label: market-neutral bar (sharpe >= 0.80 + positive cagr + >= 70% positive years at 5% borrow)

nodes.label: Muravyev, Pearson & Pollet (2025) — Why Does Options Market Information Predict Stock Returns?
nodes.rationale: Short-side predictability is largely a borrow-fee proxy: exclude hard-to-borrow names and IV-spread/skew predictability drops by at least two-thirds — i.e. the option-implied edge lives exactly where a liquidity-floored small account cannot trade.
nodes.norm_label: muravyev, pearson & pollet (2025) — why does options market information predict stock returns?

nodes.label: Crypto / 24-7 scope-expansion feasibility brief
nodes.author: Evan Daruwalla
nodes.rationale: Recommends YES to a narrowly-scoped, paper-first, liquid-only pilot on the trend/momentum edge — but explicitly NOT as a resurrection of the gap-reversal trade under a 24/7 flag. Limitation: desk research, and the key claim that reversal vanishes without closure is theory-inference across asset classes rather than a direct crypto measurement.

nodes.label: Closure manufactures the reversal edge (it is not locked treasure)
nodes.rationale: 24/7 removes the close-to-open gap but does not recover the 54% and does not remove the killer — the killer only wore the gap as a costume. Market closure itself generates short-term reversal via inventory imbalance and snap-back, so a continuous market never generates that alpha in the first place; removing closure DELETES it rather than unlocking it. The residual continuous crypto reversal is bid-ask-bounce noise, insignificant net of costs and concentrated in illiquid alts.
nodes.norm_label: closure manufactures the reversal edge (it is not locked treasure)

nodes.label: Liquidation cascade — the relocated un-catchable jump
nodes.rationale: The adverse jump reappears as an intraday, fat-tailed, alt-concentrated cascade (Oct-10-2025: -40% Solana intraday, $19B liquidated), and an 8-hour funding clock re-imposes a periodic tax on the supposedly continuous market. Being unlevered + EOD + CEX-only defuses most of it, since cascades are largely a leveraged-trader problem.
nodes.norm_label: liquidation cascade — the relocated un-catchable jump

nodes.label: Retail crypto fee reality governs viability
nodes.rationale: An EOD next-open bot is a TAKER, so the realistic Alpaca number is 25 bps/side (50 bps round trip) against the project's 10 bps round trip — 5x, with Kraken 80 bps and Coinbase up to 240 bps. The pilot must be pre-registered against crypto fees; an edge that only clears at 5 bps is a FAIL. Binance.US at ~4 bps RT is the lone exception and carries counterparty, regulatory and promotional-fee risk.
nodes.norm_label: retail crypto fee reality governs viability

nodes.label: Custody / exchange counterparty risk — the DEALBREAKER-class risk with no equity analog
nodes.rationale: 100% of capital sits uninsured on a venue that can be hacked ($1.5B Bybit 2025), freeze (Celsius) or be insolvent (FTX, Mt Gox), and it is not diversifiable at this size. Manageable only via large audited proof-of-reserve US-regulated venues plus withdrawing profits — the residual tail never reaches zero. This should be the deciding factor.
nodes.norm_label: custody / exchange counterparty risk — the dealbreaker-class risk with no equity analog

nodes.label: Wash trading + token survivorship as paired backtest-integrity threats
nodes.rationale: ~70% of reported volume is wash-traded, ~24% of tokens are pump-and-dumps, and >58% of all listed tokens are dead. A backtest that filters liquidity on REPORTED volume and runs on the surviving universe shows fictional returns — survivorship inflates crypto backtests ~17-22%/yr, up to 50-200% strategy-dependent. Manageable with point-in-time delisting-inclusive data and a depth-not-volume floor, but an automatic rigor FAIL if skipped and the most likely way to fool yourself.
nodes.norm_label: wash trading + token survivorship as paired backtest-integrity threats

nodes.label: BTC/ETH time-series trend momentum — the one WORTH-A-PREREG candidate
nodes.rationale: Liquid-native, days-to-weeks, long-or-flat — matches an EOD spot bot exactly, and 'signal at UTC bar-close, execute next bar' has ZERO gap by construction. Honest failure mode to pre-register as an expected drawdown rather than a tuning target: TS momentum went negative in the choppy 2022-23 tape.
nodes.norm_label: btc/eth time-series trend momentum — the one worth-a-prereg candidate

nodes.label: Alpaca paper trading (equity + crypto sandbox)
nodes.rationale: Lets the validation phase run at zero fee leakage and zero capital risk while honouring pre-registration — but it also fills at the full quoted half-spread with no size check, so it will hide the liquidity-floor problem if the backtest does not cap fill size.

nodes.label: Liu & Tsyvinski (2021) — Risks and Returns of Cryptocurrency
nodes.rationale: 1-4 week predictability on the majors — the evidence base for the one crypto candidate that survives.
nodes.norm_label: liu & tsyvinski (2021) — risks and returns of cryptocurrency

nodes.label: Della Corte & Kosowski — Market Closure and Short-Term Reversal
nodes.norm_label: della corte & kosowski — market closure and short-term reversal

nodes.label: Cong, Li, Tang & Yang (2022) — Crypto Wash Trading
nodes.norm_label: cong, li, tang & yang (2022) — crypto wash trading

nodes.label: Alternative & premium data cost-benefit brief
nodes.author: Evan Daruwalla
nodes.rationale: Budget framing: $100-1,000 is TRADING capital, so any $/mo feed is scoped as 'buy one month, validate the backtest, cancel' — a research cost, never a standing operating cost until capital is 10-50x larger. Honest caveat on all of it: every documented edge here concentrates in low-coverage, small, illiquid, hard-to-borrow names the floor forbids, so a clean test on a liquid universe may simply show the edge already arbitraged.

nodes.label: E17 partially unblocked FREE (FINRA exchange-listed SI from June 2021)
nodes.rationale: The E17 'wall' is real for DEEP history but overstated: pre-June-2021 free short interest is OTC-only, yet exchange-listed consolidated SI is free biweekly from June 2021 onward — ~5 years of real settlement-date data, enough to run days-to-cover as a modern out-of-sample test at zero cost. This is what became X2.
nodes.norm_label: e17 partially unblocked free (finra exchange-listed si from june 2021)

nodes.label: Option-implied signals are ~2/3 a borrow-fee proxy
nodes.rationale: The single most decisive cross-cut: IV spread and skew predict returns mostly because they proxy the stock borrow fee, and excluding hard-to-borrow names drops predictability by at least two-thirds. The edge lives exactly where a floored small account can't trade, so paying for options data would buy an inaccessible signal.
nodes.norm_label: option-implied signals are ~2/3 a borrow-fee proxy

nodes.label: PIT-fundamentals trap (silent backfill and restatement)
nodes.rationale: yfinance serves only current/restated data for the currently-listed universe, so a fundamentals time-series signal built on it carries survivorship AND look-ahead; cheap feeds (FMP/Finnhub) backfill and restate silently. Prefer event-DATED signals; clean point-in-time consensus is I/B/E/S, which is WRDS-academic-only.

nodes.label: Exotic panels — retail is the harvested counterparty
nodes.rationale: The strongest, cleanest alt-data edges are the most unaffordable (card/transaction panels $100k-1M+/yr; satellite $50k-500k/yr plus a geospatial team), and the Berkeley/RS Metrics satellite study explicitly documents retail investors as the LOSING counterparty being harvested by the funds that own the data. 'Retail tiers' are 1.5-24x the whole account and aren't the point-in-time feeds that produced the published alpha.
nodes.norm_label: exotic panels — retail is the harvested counterparty

nodes.label: Reg SHO daily short-volume (free, 2009+)
nodes.rationale: Deep, daily, single-name, point-in-time and free — but it is EXECUTED short volume contaminated by market-maker hedging, off-exchange unless each exchange's file is consolidated, and is not short interest. Overlay-grade proxy for the paid signed-flow signal.

nodes.label: Ortex Advanced (~$129/mo) — the one budget dollar
nodes.rationale: The only retail route to a proxied cost-to-borrow/utilization feed, covering both short interest and the loan-fee anomaly in one subscription — but recommended only AFTER the free tests prove the concept. X2b's borrow sweep later showed paid borrow data would not have rescued the result.
nodes.norm_label: ortex advanced (~$129/mo) — the one budget dollar

nodes.label: FMP Starter (~$22/mo) — cheapest clean event-dated test
nodes.rationale: Analyst recommendation-CHANGE drift beats numeric estimate-revision drift as a first cheap test purely because a rating change is an EVENT WITH A DATE, needing no point-in-time consensus snapshot. Its confirmed-earnings-date endpoint also fixes the E15 look-ahead concern for free, provided the date is frozen as-of the pre-event decision.
nodes.norm_label: fmp starter (~$22/mo) — cheapest clean event-dated test

nodes.label: University WRDS login escalation (I/B/E/S + Compustat PIT)
nodes.rationale: A relationship, not a purchase — free to a student and the only clean way to unblock the estimate-revision and PIT-fundamentals family. Flagged for Evan rather than worked around.
nodes.norm_label: university wrds login escalation (i/b/e/s + compustat pit)

nodes.label: Engelberg, Evans, Leonard, Reed & Ringgenberg — The Loan Fee Anomaly
nodes.rationale: 4.01%/mo long-short, Sharpe 0.66, 42% unique against 102 anomalies — the single best return predictor surveyed, and institutionally priced.
nodes.norm_label: engelberg, evans, leonard, reed & ringgenberg — the loan fee anomaly

nodes.label: Womack (1996) — Do Brokerage Analysts' Recommendations Have Investment Value?
nodes.norm_label: womack (1996) — do brokerage analysts' recommendations have investment value?

nodes.label: Gleason & Lee (2003) — Analyst Forecast Revisions and Market Price Discovery
nodes.norm_label: gleason & lee (2003) — analyst forecast revisions and market price discovery

nodes.label: Diether, Lee & Werner (2009) — Short-Sale Strategies and Return Predictability
nodes.norm_label: diether, lee & werner (2009) — short-sale strategies and return predictability

nodes.label: LLM-driven swing-trading strategies brief (~90 variants, 7 families)
nodes.author: Evan Daruwalla
nodes.rationale: H1 ('an LLM can earn a real tradable swing edge here') is rejected in its strong standalone-engine form and survives only as H1' (a risk-adjusted overlay improvement provable at a pre-registered decision-N); the null H0 survives every family. Desk research only, several 2026 preprints relayed from abstracts, and the field is publication-biased — which is itself a finding, since >70% of published LLM-trading results fail to replicate.
nodes.norm_label: llm-driven swing-trading strategies brief (~90 variants, 7 families)

nodes.label: Training-cutoff / look-ahead contamination — the killer
nodes.rationale: An LLM scoring historical text can RECALL the outcome it was trained on, so an in-sample backtest measures memorization, not forecasting, and on high-recall names it can flip the sign. Re-tested on strictly post-cutoff windows the multi-agent showcases decay 50-72% and most fail to beat buy-and-hold; a 2019-cutoff model volunteers 'COVID-19' for Sept-2019 earnings calls >25% of the time and prompt-based date-fencing does not fix it; for earnings prediction ALL apparent skill may be contamination.

nodes.label: Non-determinism vs the frozen tripwire, and its one resolution
nodes.rationale: Even at temperature 0 hosted LLMs drift (30-50% decision-flip on repeat; floating-point non-associativity across GPU kernels), so a d=+/-0.0000pp reference cannot be pinned on a live model call. The only compatible architecture — the one the project already half-built — is to log the LLM's decisions ONCE to an immutable overlay_log, freeze it, and pin the tripwire on the deterministic backtest that replays it. This makes the LLM a frozen DATA SOURCE rather than a live dependency.
nodes.norm_label: non-determinism vs the frozen tripwire, and its one resolution

nodes.label: overlay_log — immutable LLM decision log
nodes.rationale: The freeze point that reconciles a stochastic model with a byte-exact tripwire; extended by a PnL journal in the reflection variants and by an exit_log for the exit-supervisor arm.

nodes.label: e1_control — mechanical control arm
nodes.rationale: Every LLM arm must be run as a TREATMENT against this mechanical control, never as a standalone claim.

nodes.label: e1_llm_veto — LLM overlay treatment arm
nodes.rationale: The existing binary veto is already a degenerate meta-label, so the graded-size and meta-labeling proposals nest inside it rather than requiring new machinery.

nodes.label: LLMs are demonstrably weak at reading price trends
nodes.rationale: Frontier vision-LLMs score 49-53% on candlestick direction (about chance) and the best time-series foundation models beat a random walk in only 2 of 10 return tasks with small, sparse gains. This collides with the project's own chart-TA-dies-on-cost-and-snooping prior: asking an LLM to read a chart adds model bias on top of an already-dead signal.
nodes.norm_label: llms are demonstrably weak at reading price trends

nodes.label: The genuine residual edge lives where this project can't trade and decays with adoption
nodes.rationale: The most careful positive result concentrates in small-cap and negative-news names the liquidity floor excludes, and its own authors report the edge decaying as LLM adoption rises and collapsing from ~350% to ~50% between 10 and 25 bps of cost.
nodes.norm_label: the genuine residual edge lives where this project can't trade and decays with adoption

nodes.label: E4 — LLM as offline hypothesis/rule generator (shortlist #1)
nodes.rationale: The LLM brainstorms rules, a human pre-registers one, and a deterministic backtester falsifies it — keeping the stochastic model entirely OUTSIDE the reproducibility-critical path. Zero new infra, zero tripwire risk. Not a tradable strategy itself: its value is idea-throughput, and it is literally what this brief's own agents did.
nodes.norm_label: e4 — llm as offline hypothesis/rule generator (shortlist #1)

nodes.label: D3 — triple-barrier meta-labeler (shortlist #2)
nodes.rationale: Best-evidenced overlay (precision 0.21 -> 0.39 in the reference study). Fundamental limit: an overlay can only improve a PROFITABLE base signal, and the project's base signals mostly failed — so it needs a live or borderline base to sit on.

nodes.label: Infra & compute ladder (Tiers 0-4)
nodes.rationale: At $100-1,000 the per-decision API cost is a FIRST-ORDER term: Tier 0 offline batch and Tier 1 human-run runbook need no API key and are tripwire-best; Tier 2 unattended API is BLOCKED-ON-EVAN (no key) at ~$65/yr for Opus x3 = 6.5% of a $1k book; Tier 4 multi-agent runs $5-30+/decision, roughly $2,500/yr, exceeding the entire capital.

nodes.label: Mandatory gates for any LLM experiment
nodes.rationale: Non-optional: evaluate strictly AFTER the pinned model's knowledge cutoff; anonymize tickers to kill the distraction effect; run a look-ahead/fake-date placebo audit; pin the exact model ID because a silent upgrade moves the cutoff and re-contaminates the 'clean' window; run as treatment vs the mechanical control; account for Tier 0/1 cost.
nodes.norm_label: mandatory gates for any llm experiment
