nodes.label: check_feed_clock()
nodes.rationale: Returns the refusal reason or None; called at daily_swing_paper.py:733-754 BEFORE the VIX/VIX3M fetches so a refusal costs no network. Refuses in BOTH directions: feed behind is the real bug, feed ahead is a partial row or a wrong calendar.

nodes.label: Why Not Alpaca's Calendar API
nodes.rationale: Asked and answered: the M3 DB ledger is independent of broker connectivity by design and a total credential outage is a logged real event, so an Alpaca-sourced clock would turn that outage into a refusal to mark NAV, manufacturing the very holes the guard exists to prevent.

nodes.label: paper_sleeves.divergence_census()
nodes.rationale: Buckets every fill_divergence row (measured / resolved_no_price / dark / pending, mutually exclusive, summing to total) and lives beside open_divergence_rows, whose alpaca_order_id IS NOT NULL clause creates the darkness.

nodes.label: Report Split From Resolving, Ungated On Purpose
nodes.rationale: print_divergence_census() is called UNGATED at :824 beside the missed-session detector; tidying it into backfill_divergence would move it inside if args.execute: and delete it from every dry run, which is exactly what M13.3 required it to survive.
nodes.norm_label: report split from resolving, ungated on purpose

nodes.label: Two-Doc Project Memory System
nodes.rationale: HANDOFF.md as the only live snapshot plus an append-only record in docs/, PRD_ROADMAP.md and these bins; absolute dates everywhere.

nodes.label: Adjustment-Convention Header Rule
nodes.rationale: Any script touching price data states its adjustment convention in a header comment (project CLAUDE.md rule).

nodes.label: Frozen-Regression-Test Pattern
nodes.rationale: Pinned reference numbers, own __main__, fail loud on drift; ported from Trading's trading_bot/strategies/test_strategies.py. Planned at bootstrap, DONE since 2026-07-09, and the tolerance is tighter than the original bullet described.

nodes.label: Record Correction Sub-Head Rule
nodes.rationale: Corrections are written as '## <X>-note - ...' sub-heads, NEVER as '# Appendix <X>-note - ...'; the latter is unparseable and wedges every future append. A top-level Appendix heading must use a fresh unused letter with no suffix.

nodes.label: Dated Exception Pattern
nodes.rationale: A hard rule the code must contradict gets a DATED EXCEPTION in CLAUDE.md plus a pointer comment at the code line, stating its scope and its reversal path - never a silent divergence and never a fix that breaks the evidence.

nodes.label: STRESS_K = 4 Dated Exception
nodes.rationale: paper_sleeves.py:43 exceeds the K=1-3 ceiling because K=4 is the parameter C1 and M10-1 were backtested at; dropping to 3 would make the live sleeve run a rule no backtest has tested. Scope: the M10-1 stress branch only. Reversal: re-run both at K=3 under a fresh prereg.

nodes.label: swing_bot/prices.py
nodes.rationale: The own yfinance fetcher: full OHLCV with auto_adjust=False into swing.db. fetch() has NO cache - a bare yf.download per call with a retry ladder - so M3 feed staleness is always the vendor, never a local cache.

nodes.label: swing.db bars Table
nodes.rationale: PK (ticker,date) with open/high/low/close/adj_close/volume; also holds positions, NAV and results from M3 on. Spans 2014-01-02 to 2026-07-08, 105,396 rows over 34 tickers.

nodes.label: Split-Adjusted, Dividend-UNadjusted Convention
nodes.rationale: auto_adjust=False. Every consumer must honor it or returns are silently wrong, and every script touching price data states it in a header comment.

nodes.label: .e8e9_cache Research Store
nodes.rationale: The second data layer: gitignored, 292 files in ONE filename namespace over THREE shapes - 181 bar lists, 72 dicts (*_div, ff3_daily, *_idx, fred_*), 39 lists of date strings (*_earn). Only bar lists carry a vintage, so 111 files are invisible to the freshness guard BY DESIGN. Spans 1998-12-22 to 2026-08-17.

nodes.label: scripts/run_e8_squeeze.py
nodes.rationale: Owns the repo's real shared data layer for the experiment jungle; 31 files import the module, 28 of them naming cache_fetch.

nodes.label: cache_fetch()
nodes.rationale: Permanent on-disk yfinance cache feeding the EXPERIMENTS, while prices.py -> swing.db feeds the ENGINES and the live M3 loop. Same adjustment convention. Retries on a 20/40/60/80 s ladder per ticker on a miss.

nodes.label: _note_vintage()
nodes.rationale: Raises StaleCacheError on a mixed vintage (2+ distinct end-dates in one process) or a stale one; mixed fires BEFORE stale. Returns early for dict-shaped files because _last_bar_date is None for them.

nodes.label: StaleCacheError
nodes.rationale: A named RuntimeError subclass, created so consumers could re-raise the verdict explicitly instead of swallowing it in a broad except.

nodes.label: Cache Freshness Contract
nodes.rationale: Entries are written on whatever day a ticker is first touched, so a universe assembled across sessions silently MIXES VINTAGES - which is what overstated M12's headline effect 3x. Refreshing is all-or-nothing: the write path is per-ticker and cache-miss-driven, no script enumerates the cache, and deleting a subset just manufactures a new mixed vintage.

nodes.label: EOD-Only Invariant
nodes.rationale: Signal at close, execute next open. No intraday logic until an intraday data source exists.

nodes.label: Mandatory Liquidity Floor
nodes.rationale: Mandatory in any universe filter because at $100-1,000 capital spread and slippage dominate. Enforced in the research runners (E1, E8, E9, E11, E12, C3, E20, X9) only since 2026-09-05 - the invariant was true nowhere in research before that.

nodes.label: paper_nav Table
nodes.rationale: Primary key is (sleeve, date). Never aggregate it to a bare date set for a completeness check; coverage questions are per-sleeve questions.

nodes.label: Unequal Sleeve NAV Series
nodes.rationale: At 2026-09-05: e18_vixts 36 marks, m10_1_nagel 36, e6_1x 31 (103 rows total). Any cross-sleeve return or NAV comparison MUST align on dates and must never assume equal series.

nodes.label: ACKNOWLEDGED_NAV_HOLES
nodes.rationale: The (sleeve, date) pairs in daily_swing_paper.py for holes accepted as PERMANENT (Evan, 2026-09-05): forward evidence is not reconstructed after the fact. Still printed every run but no longer failing it. They had to become pairs because a date-scoped acknowledgement forgives that date for every sleeve.

nodes.label: Unattributed Ledger Write Caveat
nodes.rationale: One unattributed write to the live ledger after 2026-09-01, bounded to two provably synthetic rows left on 2026-08-25 (a fake paper_nav row implying a QQQ close of 812.00 against the same day's real ~710.7, and a ZZZZ position with no matching transactions). Deletions match clean_ledger_2026-08-25.py exactly and the row arithmetic reconciles; what happened is known and surgical, who ran it and when is not.

nodes.label: Two Price Stores, Different Windows
nodes.rationale: Results from one are NOT comparable to the other. Measured in F3: under the same floor swing.db shows 6 of 29 names with a sub-floor bar (635 bars) while .e8e9_cache shows 27 of 29 (38,573 bars) - the difference is entirely the 2000s, where the ETF illiquidity lives. Any claim about how often the floor binds must name its store.

nodes.label: adj_close Dual Price Convention
nodes.rationale: In .e8e9_cache bars, close (idx 5) is split-adjusted and dividend-UNadjusted while adj_close (idx 6) is split+dividend adjusted and 100% populated. Yahoo back-adjusts the whole history so adj/close runs 0.5488 at SPY's 1993 start to exactly 1.0 on the newest bar; splits cancel in that ratio, isolating dividends.

nodes.label: Multiplicative Dividend Adjustment
nodes.rationale: k = 1/(1 - D/close[t-1]), verified across 135 SPY ex-dates at median relative error 3.5e-5. It is not additive, and adj_close differencing is not a usable ex-date detector because float32 quantization moves the ratio on 8,307 of 8,443 SPY days - threshold at 0.05 bps.

nodes.label: broad_us History Depth
nodes.rationale: At vintage 2026-08-17: SPY 8,444 bars from 1993-01-29, DIA 7,188 from 1998-01-20, QQQ 6,902 from 1999-03-10, IWM 6,594 from 2000-05-26. Any study needing pre-2014 depth must use the cache, not swing.db.

nodes.label: Python 3.14.4
nodes.rationale: Runs in .venv. If a pandas/numpy edge breaks a milestone, revisit the Python version rather than coding around it (record Appendix E).

nodes.label: requirements.txt
nodes.rationale: Direct pins, pinned 2026-07-08; re-pinned after any dependency change.

nodes.label: yfinance 1.5.1
nodes.rationale: The vendor behind the own price fetcher.

nodes.label: pandas 3.0.3 / numpy 2.5.1
nodes.rationale: Bleeding-edge majors; pandas 3.0.x changes defaults, which is the edge the dependencies header warns about.

nodes.label: ST-2 Direct-Import Re-Pin
nodes.rationale: pandas and numpy are DIRECT imports (run_c1_residual_reversal.py, run_e10_earnings_drift.py) that were pinned only in the lock's transitive freeze, so a clean-machine pip install -r requirements.txt would have resolved them to whatever was newest, straight into the pandas-3.0.x default-changing edge.

nodes.label: scripts/render_record_html.py
nodes.rationale: Direct markdown 3.10.3 import at line 30; renders the append-only record to a standalone HTML twin.

nodes.label: pytest Is Optional
nodes.rationale: Frozen-regression tests run via their own __main__, matching Trading's pattern; pytest is not installed and not required.

nodes.label: Public Repo Under Evan's Real Name
nodes.rationale: github.com/Evan-Daruwalla/Swing-Trading-Project, public since 2026-07-10 as a college-application portfolio piece. The default is inverted from a private repo: anything committed is world-readable permanently, because git history survives a later deletion.
nodes.norm_label: public repo under evan's real name

nodes.label: The Resume Test
nodes.rationale: Ask 'would I put this on a resume' before git add, not after - because the scanners can judge secrets but not embarrassment.

nodes.label: trading-guard Push Block
nodes.rationale: A hook blocks the model from running git push at all; publishing is Evan's call and the block is not to be worked around.

nodes.label: The Never-Leaves Hard Line
nodes.rationale: Alpaca key pairs, swing.db (the live paper ledger), var/ runtime logs, and any live brokerage account number or anything from a non-paper account.

nodes.label: .gitignore
nodes.rationale: Enforces the hard line: *_keys.env and *.env cover alpaca_keys.env; swing.db plus journal/wal/shm; var/; .e8e9_cache/; the research caches; graphify-out/cache/.

nodes.label: alpaca_client._require_paper()
nodes.rationale: Refuses live endpoints; no live account exists and this project has never traded real money.

nodes.label: Missing .claude/secrets-inventory.md
nodes.rationale: commit-gate reads that file and this project has never had it. The scanners still run on their built-in rules so nothing is unguarded, but the project-specific inventory they would consult is absent. Left unfixed deliberately: writing it is a security decision, not a bookkeeping one.

nodes.label: Every Failed Experiment Published
nodes.rationale: The 37-attempt search phase, the falsified predictions and the retracted claims are all public on purpose - a failure honestly recorded is the deliverable.

nodes.label: Synthetic Identifiers In New Fixtures
nodes.rationale: prove_divergence_census.py originally seeded its throwaway DB with five real 8-char order-id prefixes; the census only tests NULL vs NOT NULL so they added nothing, and they became oid-1..oid-5. Rule: 'already published elsewhere' is not a reason to publish again in a new file - only need is. Prices were kept real because they make the arithmetic checkable.

nodes.label: The 30-Second Pre-Push Check
nodes.rationale: git diff --cached --stat, git ls-files --others --exclude-standard, and a grep of the staged diff for key/secret/token/password and long uppercase runs - done by eye because the scan cannot judge embarrassment.

nodes.label: swing_bot/paper_sleeves.py
nodes.rationale: Holds the M3 ledger and the per-sleeve decision functions decide_e6_1x, decide_e18_vixts and decide_m10_1.

nodes.label: Three Live Paper Sleeves
nodes.rationale: Running live in paper since 2026-07-15, each its own $1,000 Alpaca PAPER account.

nodes.label: e6_1x Sleeve
nodes.rationale: QQQ versus its 200-DMA. Has 31 NAV marks against its peers' 36.

nodes.label: e18_vixts Sleeve
nodes.rationale: A VIX/VIX3M term-structure gate.

nodes.label: m10_1_nagel Sleeve
nodes.rationale: VIX>20 selects the C1 residual reversal, otherwise the E6 trend; weekly, on Fridays.

nodes.label: Sleeve Reuses Its Backtest's Condition
nodes.rationale: Each live decision function reuses the IDENTICAL condition as its backtest runner, so the live code and the tested code cannot diverge.

nodes.label: Forward Evidence, Not Validated Edges
nodes.rationale: Nothing has passed the high-return bar; the sleeves exist to accumulate forward evidence, and they are not claimed as validated edges.

nodes.label: Inherited yfinance Traps
nodes.rationale: Inherited 2026-07-08 from Trading's battle scars: split misapplication (a >1000% single-day move is the tell), incomplete same-day publication (~4,400 of 5,200 tickers that never settles, so gate freshness on coverage COUNT not on 'ran today'), Friday-spike corruption and multi-year cache-gap phantom ranking.

nodes.label: Survivorship Bias
nodes.rationale: yfinance carries currently-listed names only, so every backtest is upper-bound-biased. Short-horizon mean reversion is worst hit, since delisted crashers are exactly what an RSI<30 buyer catches. No fix exists in the current stack; state it in every result.

nodes.label: Fixed Initial-Capital/K Position Sizing
nodes.rationale: backtest.py sizes at fixed initial-capital/K dollars, NOT current-NAV/K, so after losses it keeps buying full size (implicit leverage; cash can go negative). At K=1 on 3x funds NAV crossed zero, maxDD 104%. Does not invalidate the pinned refs since all experiments shared these semantics, but any FUTURE engine or live loop must size on current NAV.

nodes.label: XLRE Zero-Range Bars
nodes.rationale: 19 High==High bars in 2015-10..2016-02, XLRE's first ~5 months post-launch (illiquid early trading, not a split error). IBS=(close-low)/(high-low) divides by zero on these, so signal code must treat IBS as undefined and emit no signal rather than crash. All 28 other universe tickers were clean in the M0.4 scan.

nodes.label: coverage_gate.sanity_scan
nodes.rationale: The detector for OHLC-order violations, |daily ret|>35% and zero-range bars.

nodes.label: A raise Is Inert Until You Check What Catches It
nodes.rationale: _note_vintage was proven to fire 5/5 in isolation yet was swallowed at three reachable sites - worst inside cache_fetch's own retry loop, where a vintage verdict printed as an attempt error, slept 20/40/60/80s, refetched 4x and died as 'could not fetch'. Two consumers caught it per-ticker and continued, so a uniformly stale cache excluded every name in turn: the guard turned 'refuse to run' into 'run on a silently emptied universe'. Rule: a broad except around a call that can now raise a VERDICT must re-raise that verdict explicitly.
nodes.norm_label: a raise is inert until you check what catches it

nodes.label: scripts/ Is An Implicit Namespace Package
nodes.rationale: No __init__.py and the repo root on sys.path, so import run_e8_squeeze and import scripts.run_e8_squeeze both succeed and produce TWO module objects with two different StaleCacheError classes - except StaleCacheError then silently does not match. Today's consumers are safe (proven by identity, is returns True; zero repo-wide hits for the dotted form). Rule: import sibling scripts as bare run_x, never scripts.run_x.
nodes.norm_label: scripts/ is an implicit namespace package

nodes.label: Aggregation Collapse On A Composite Key
nodes.rationale: The missed-session detector read SELECT DISTINCT date FROM paper_nav whose PK is (sleeve,date), so a date counted as covered when ANY ONE sleeve wrote it; it printed clean for 11 nights while e6_1x recorded nothing for five sessions. The one real vanish it ever had to catch was the one kind it structurally could not see. Rule: never DISTINCT one column of a composite key and then treat presence as coverage.
nodes.norm_label: aggregation collapse on a composite key

nodes.label: A Fail-Open Guard Written Into A Docstring
nodes.rationale: median_dollar_volume() returned None below max(5, n//2) usable sessions and its docstring told callers not to treat that as illiquid; the one caller obeyed, so a data-starved name skipped the floor entirely and could enter the live K=4 stress basket. Fixing only the call site would have left the next caller reading instructions to re-introduce it. Rule: when a helper returns 'unknown', its docstring must say FAIL CLOSED.
nodes.norm_label: a fail-open guard written into a docstring

nodes.label: One Malformed Heading Wedges Every Append
nodes.rationale: '# Appendix BR-note - ...' does not match the letter scan, so append-record-entry.js refused every append for 54 days - which is why the 2026-09-05 scheduled audit left no trace. The refusal is correct but only visible at write time; fixing it exposed a second wedge, a TOC invariant refusing with 36 TOC lines against 167 appendix headings.
nodes.norm_label: one malformed heading wedges every append

nodes.label: A Filter Can Destroy A Verdict By Starving The Sample
nodes.rationale: The liquidity floor cut E11's gate sample from 46 closed trades to 24, under its own pre-registered n>=30 minimum, so E11 stopped returning FAIL and started returning INCONCLUSIVE - it lost the right to a verdict. Rule: check post-screen n against the experiment's own minimum BEFORE reading its metrics, or a sample-size failure gets read as a performance result.
nodes.norm_label: a filter can destroy a verdict by starving the sample

nodes.label: Candidate Supply Governs Screen Impact
nodes.rationale: Three pre-registered predictions reasoned from mechanics - hold duration, selection style, pool size - and all three were wrong: E9 moved least (-1.9%), E20 moved -14%, and X9 traded MORE (2,196 -> 2,502 opens) because removing names changes which pairs are the K=3 lowest-SSD. A screen's impact tracks how many candidates a strategy had to begin with.

nodes.label: A Detector Whose Clock Comes From The Feed It Checks
nodes.rationale: daily_swing_paper.py set today = qdates[-1] from series('QQQ'), so from 2026-09-02 the 19:00 run found no same-day bar and silently processed the previous session three runs in a row after a 17-run same-day streak. The per-sleeve missed-session detector excludes today by design and its today was the same lagged value, so it reported clean. Rule: the expected session date must come from an INDEPENDENT source, and a feed behind it is a refusal, not a substitution.
nodes.norm_label: a detector whose clock comes from the feed it checks

nodes.label: The Guard-That-Cannot-Fire Family
nodes.rationale: This project's recurring defect class, at eight variants by 2026-09-05: a guard that exists, looks correct, and is structurally incapable of firing on the case it was written for.

nodes.label: The Convention Guard Greps The Whole File
nodes.rationale: _price_scripts_missing_convention_header counts a file as price-touching if the bare word yfinance appears ANYWHERE in it, prose included, but requires the convention string in the first 40 lines - so a module that merely mentions yfinance goes RED. Fix by stating the convention truthfully in the header, never by editing the invariant.
nodes.norm_label: the convention guard greps the whole file

nodes.label: The Ex-Dividend Drop Falls In The Overnight Window
nodes.rationale: On dividend-UNadjusted prices the drop lands entirely in close[t-1] -> open[t], so a close-to-open vs open-to-close decomposition run on close alone understates the overnight leg by the whole dividend yield: ~183 bps/yr on SPY, ~51 on QQQ, and DIFFERENTIAL across tickers, so a price-only cross-ticker table measures dividend policy, not drift. The correct form is multiplicative; the additive DIV = TR - PR form breaks by the cross term DIV*ID, up to 154 bps over SPY's history.
nodes.norm_label: the ex-dividend drop falls in the overnight window

nodes.label: *_div.json Is Never Vintage-Checked
nodes.rationale: _last_bar_date returns None for dict-shaped files so _note_vintage returns early and the staleness guard skips them; the div files are vintage 2026-07-11 against 2026-08-18 bars, and DIA's 2026-07-17 ex-date is in adj_close but absent from DIA_div.json. Use adj_close differencing as the primary dividend source.

nodes.label: An Era Comparison On A 10.6%-Vol Series Is Underpowered ~40x
nodes.rationale: Post-2022 (n=1,159) the 95% CI on SPY's overnight drift is +-9.57 pp/yr against a 1-2 pp/yr effect; 2-sigma resolution needs ~200 years. Comparing a 4.6y window to a 29y window is not a test either, since the long window's SE is ~5x tighter. The fair form is the percentile of the current window among all overlapping windows of the SAME length, descriptive only.
nodes.norm_label: an era comparison on a 10.6%-vol series is underpowered ~40x

nodes.label: F3 Sweep Measured Runtimes
nodes.rationale: Measured on this machine with a warm cache: run_e8_squeeze 2.2 s per full run (29 ETFs, 2000->), E9/E11/E12 comparable, run_c3_vol_breakout ~60 s per arm (five rung/arm variants), E20 and X9 each under 10 s. One complete sweep - 8 experiments x 2 arms x 2 repeats for determinism = 32 runs - finished in under 5 minutes, and liquidity_mask over 29 series x ~6,500 bars adds no measurable time.

nodes.label: A Cold Cache Dominates The Cost
nodes.rationale: The retry ladder is 20/40/60/80 s per ticker on a miss, which swamps every measured engine runtime.
nodes.norm_label: a cold cache dominates the cost

nodes.label: alpaca_keys.env
nodes.rationale: At the repo root: three per-sleeve Alpaca PAPER key pairs, untracked and ignored via .gitignore:18 (*.env), never tracked on any branch - git log --all -- alpaca_keys.env is empty.

nodes.label: Gitignored Keys-File Pattern
nodes.rationale: Inherited from Trading: keys live in a gitignored .env loaded by a no-dep loader, never committed, never echoed to chat.

nodes.label: swing_bot/alpaca_client.py
nodes.rationale: The broker client, ported from Trading with its live-trading guard intact.

nodes.label: is_live() Hard Guard
nodes.rationale: Trading's client hard-guards live trading; any client ported here must keep the guard. The PAPER base URL is the default and live is opt-in and currently out of scope entirely.

nodes.label: scripts/git-hooks/pre-commit
nodes.rationale: Reached by core.hooksPath and covering SHELL-made commits. It runs a secret scan AND the record's append-only and TOC-balance invariants, and blocks the commit on failure; verified live 2026-08-18 and it fired for real on 2026-09-05 with 'APPEND-ONLY VIOLATION', with the commit going through only on a disclosed --no-verify on Evan's explicit call.

nodes.label: commit-gate Canonical pre-commit
nodes.rationale: The shared hook the project hook delegates to.

nodes.label: PreToolUse Commit Gate
nodes.rationale: Covers MODEL-made commits and predates the native hook.

nodes.label: The Shell-Path-Only Pre-Fix Exposure
nodes.rationale: Before 2026-08-16, core.hooksPath was unset and no .git/hooks/pre-commit existed, so a shell-made commit ran no scanner - but model-made commits were already gated, so the exposure was the shell path only, NOT 'no scanner on any commit' as the audit finding first stated.

nodes.label: swing_bot/test_frozen.py
nodes.rationale: The tripwire: two kinds of case in one file, no framework, own __main__ - Trading's pattern.

nodes.label: FROZEN TESTS: GREEN Done-Check
nodes.rationale: python -m swing_bot.test_frozen must print GREEN (all d=0), run after ANY change to swing_bot/ or to scripts/daily_swing_paper.py. A non-zero d is a FAIL, not a discussion - the references are pinned precisely so drift is loud.

nodes.label: 12 Pinned References
nodes.rationale: E1/E1b/E2 total-PnL and closed-trade counts on fixed swing.db windows plus E4 rotation, declared to +-0.0000pp, running the real engine against the real bars table opened READ-ONLY.

nodes.label: 19 Pure-Function Invariants
nodes.rationale: 17 until 2026-09-06, when audit FX added e18_zero_vix_refuses and e18_negative_vix_refuses. They cover signals.ibs edge cases, the three live sleeve decisions, the orchestrator's pure helpers (qty_reconcile_orders drift band and pending suppression, median_dollar_volume thin-sample refusal, isoweek_str), and the adjustment-convention header check.

nodes.label: price_scripts_state_adjustment_convention
nodes.rationale: Every scripts/*.py that imports swing_bot.prices or mentions cache_fetch must state the adjustment convention in its FIRST 40 LINES; adding a price-touching script without that header FAILS the suite, which is the intended behaviour.

nodes.label: scripts/prove_cache_guard.py
nodes.rationale: 8/8. Feeds the .e8e9_cache freshness guard its own trigger at every site that can swallow it; run it after any change to _note_vintage, cache_fetch's retry loop, or a consumer's except around cache_fetch.

nodes.label: scripts/prove_liquidity_floor.py
nodes.rationale: 11/11 since F3 (6/6 before). Pure in-memory - no DB, no network, no orders. Two cases assert the PRE-FIX branch ranked the data-starved names so a silent revert is still caught, and F3 added liquidity_mask cases: fail-closed over the first 9 indices, PAST-ONLY masking, and a mid-series feed death returning False rather than coasting on an old median.

nodes.label: Pass Counts Must Be Derived, Not Written
nodes.rationale: The first version printed 'GREEN (12/12)' while 11 cases ran, because the total was a literal. A checker that miscounts itself is not a checker.
nodes.norm_label: pass counts must be derived, not written

nodes.label: Determinism Is Part Of The F3 Protocol
nodes.rationale: Every experiment arm is run twice and the two outputs must be byte-identical before any comparison is believed; all 16 runs (8 experiments x 2 arms) passed.
nodes.norm_label: determinism is part of the f3 protocol

nodes.label: scripts/prove_torn_write.py
nodes.rationale: PROVEN: 32 checks. Arms A and F are what make it a proof: A reproduces the pre-fix shape and requires the harness to DETECT the tear, and F is an ast walk asserting all 5 ledger calls carry commit=False inside a with conn: and that there are exactly TWO transactions, so a later edit cannot silently un-defer a write. The assertion is a LEDGER REPLAY, not row counts - replay every paper_transactions row from the opening state and require equality with stored cash and positions to 1e-9.

nodes.label: It Kills A Real Child Process, It Does Not raise
nodes.rationale: An in-process raise only shows with conn: unwinding cleanly; it does not model ExecutionTimeLimit or a reboot. Each kill arm re-execs the file as a child that monkeypatches one paper_sleeves function to os._exit(137) - no __exit__, no atexit, no close() - then the parent reopens the DB and lets SQLite's rollback journal decide, asserting the child's return code is exactly 137 so a child that merely errored cannot pass as a kill.
nodes.norm_label: it kills a real child process, it does not raise

nodes.label: Arm G Pins A Toolchain Fact
nodes.rationale: An inner conn.commit() ENDS a transaction opened by with conn:, so wrapping self-committing writes is a no-op - which is why the audit's own prescribed fix would not have worked. It is now a runnable check rather than prose.
nodes.norm_label: arm g pins a toolchain fact

nodes.label: realize_pending()
nodes.rationale: Its ledger writes are atomic PER PHASE, and there are exactly two transactions.

nodes.label: scripts/prove_feed_clock.py
nodes.rationale: PROVEN: 18 checks, exit 0. No DB, no network, no clock dependence - every case pins an explicit now. Coverage: the real incident replayed, the Labor Day run, a before-close run, Good Friday, the Jul-4-observed-Friday shift, a 4-session stall, feed-ahead, and three observance shifts including Dec 31 2021 still TRADING. The derived 2026 closure list is printed for eyeballing rather than asserted from memory.

nodes.label: A Proof Must Call The Shipped Function
nodes.rationale: prove_feed_clock calls the same check_feed_clock the live loop calls, not a copy of the branch, so the proof cannot drift away from the shipped guard - whereas prove_liquidity_floor had to duplicate its branch. Proving the function is still not proving the call site: a separate scratchpad landing check ran _run() on a throwaway DB with series() monkeypatched and confirmed exit 1 with 0 rows written.
nodes.norm_label: a proof must call the shipped function

nodes.label: scripts/prove_divergence_census.py
nodes.rationale: PROVEN: 16 checks. Seeds a throwaway DB with the live fill_divergence table's exact shape; swing.db is never opened and no network is touched. Part B parses daily_swing_paper.py with ast, walks _run, and asserts print_divergence_census is NOT nested under any if args.execute: while backfill_divergence still IS - a 'this line must appear on a dry run' requirement is otherwise checkable only by running the live loop, which this project forbids in a dev session. nodes.label: verdicts(raw_last, filtered_last, expected)
